title: What UVM assets and findings are, what the Assets and Findings pages show, and how on-demand asset scans work

prose.text: The contents of the entity drawers are open {{gap:drawer-tabs}}.

asset-definition.statement: A UVM asset represents a single asset in the environment, unified (merged) and enriched with information from multiple sources; the Assets page lets users see the sources and records it was merged from, its findings and its related tickets.

quotes: Each asset represents a single asset in your environment, unified (i.e., merged) and enriched with information from multiple sources.
view the sources and records from which it was merged, view the findings it contains, and view the tickets it's related to.

asset-risk-score.statement: On the Assets page, Risk Score reflects the highest severity score among the asset's findings and is initially set by the default reconciliation function, which can be customized through Data Unification; Risk Mass is the sum of severity scores of the asset's active findings.

quotes: The risk score is initially set by the default reconciliation function, and reflects the highest severity score among the findings. The default can be customized through Data Unification.
Risk Mass: The sum of all severity scores of the active findings associated with the asset.

asset-crown-jewel.statement: Is Crown Jewel is a boolean (TRUE or FALSE) field indicating whether the asset is defined as one of the organization's most valuable assets, and Assets can be filtered by Asset Is Crown Jewel, State, Owner ID or Source.

quotes: Is Crown Jewel: A boolean field with values of TRUE or FALSE indicating whether the asset is defined as a crown jewel asset (i.e., one of your organization's most valuable assets).
Filter assets by Asset Is Crown Jewel, State, Owner ID, or Source.

asset-charts.statement: The Assets overview charts show assets by risk score in increments of 0.5 (X-axis the max severity score of active findings) and the 5 most frequent asset types and operating systems.

quotes: The X-axis represents the max severity score of active findings related to the asset
Displays the number of assets in the different risk score ranges (in increments of 0.5).
Presents asset count categorized by asset type, displaying the 5 most frequently occurring types.
Displays the number of assets categorized by operating system, displaying the 5 most frequently occurring types.

asset-columns.statement: With the default Active saved view selected, the details shown for each asset include Total Findings (the sum of active findings per severity), First Seen and Last Seen (earliest and latest finding detection dates on the asset), and Tags pulled from sources.

quotes: When the default Active saved view is selected, you can see the following details for each asset:
Total Findings: The sum of the active findings per severity.
First Seen: The earliest date on which a finding on the asset was first detected.
Last Seen: The latest date on which a finding on the asset was detected.
Tags: Tags pulled from your sources that include information about the asset that can be extracted and used to enrich the asset data.

easm-asset-types.statement: EASM-discovered assets are shown by selecting EASM Assets in the Sources filter, and the Available Asset Types listed are Certificate (SSL/TLS certificates), Domain (domains, subdomains and hosts), Edge Server (IP addresses) and Git Repository (GitHub repositories).

quotes: To view the assets discovered by Zscaler's External Attack Surface Management (EASM) capabilities, click the Sources filter and select EASM Assets.
Available Asset Types
Certificate: Includes SSL/TLS certificates.
Domain: Includes domains, subdomains, and hosts.
Edge Server: Includes IP addresses.
Git Repository: Includes GitHub repositories.

finding-definition.statement: A UVM finding is a vulnerability or misconfiguration detected on an asset and contextualized from multiple sources (such as CVE details, exposed secrets or misconfigurations); findings are grouped into tickets.

quotes: Each finding represents a vulnerability or misconfiguration detected on an asset and contextualized with additional information from multiple sources, such as CVE details, exposed secrets, or misconfigurations.
Findings are grouped into tickets based on factors like remediation teams or the affected product.

findings-charts.statement: The Findings overview compares original severity scores with recalculated contextualized scores per severity category, shows the top 5 sources by finding count, and a Finding Duplication chart of findings retrieved from different sources.

quotes: comparing their original severity scores (left bar) to recalculated contextualized scores (right bar) for each severity category.
Displays the number of findings grouped by source, showing the top 5 most frequently occurring sources.
Finding Duplication: Details the number of findings retrieved from different sources

findings-create-ticket.statement: Create Ticket on the Findings page splits the selected findings from their current ticket into a new ticket that is locked, with the originating tickets listed on its Related Tickets tab.

quotes: Create a ticket to split the selected findings from their current ticket, and adds them to a new ticket. The new ticket is locked, and the tickets that the findings originate from are listed on the new ticket's Related Tickets tab.

finding-types.statement: The Viewing Findings in UVM article lists Available Finding Types: CVE (vulnerabilities, commonly exploited CVEs and vulnerabilities supported by Threat Intelligence decoys in Zscaler Deception) and Misconfig (misconfigurations and exposures).

quotes: Available Finding Types
CVE: Includes vulnerabilities detected on assets, such as CVEs, commonly exploited CVEs, and vulnerabilities supported by Threat Intelligence (TI) decoys in Zscaler Deception.
Misconfig: Includes various misconfigurations and exposures detected on assets, including:

misconfig-list.statement: The Misconfig finding type includes exposed VPN appliances, exposed sensitive services, revealing hostnames, non-default or unknown open ports, expired domain registrations, domains with registration expiring within 30 days, expired SSL/TLS certificates, outdated SSL/TLS versions, self-signed certificates, SSL/TLS certificates expiring within 30 days, HTTP using insecure header, HTTP missing common security header and dangling DNS records.

quotes: Exposed VPN appliances
Non-default or unknown open ports
Domains with registration expiring within 30 days
SSL/TLS certificates expiring within 30 days
HTTP missing common security header
Dangling DNS records
Self-signed certificates
Outdated SSL/TLS versions
Expired SSL/TLS certificates
Expired domain registrations
Revealing hostnames
Exposed sensitive services
HTTP using insecure header

finding-evidence.statement: The finding drawer's Finding Evidence tab information is only available for findings ingested using Zscaler's EASM capabilities, and shows the Scan Output (labeled by scan type, such as HTTP Response, Nmap Response and Certificate Response) and Match Evidence, the portions of the scan results that attest to the finding.

quotes: This information is only available for findings ingested using Zscaler's EASM capabilities.

Scan Output: The complete output of the scan that was used to identify the finding. This section is labeled differently for assets depending on the type of scan performed (e.g., HTTP Response, Nmap Response, and Certificate Response).
Match Evidence: The specific portions of the scan results that attest to the finding.

easm-findings-filter.statement: EASM-discovered findings are shown by selecting EASM Findings in the Sources filter.

quotes: click the Sources filter and select EASM Findings.

scan-feature-prereq.statement: On-demand asset scans from UVM are in limited availability (contact Zscaler Support) and need assets ingested by a configured data source connector, an active scanner outegration, and Read and Edit permissions under the Vulnerabilities App - Asset Operational View resource.

quotes: This feature is in limited availability. To learn more, contact Zscaler Support.
The assets you intend to scan must be ingested and managed by a configured data source connector.
You must have a configured and active scanner outegration to perform the scan.
Your assigned role must include the Read and Edit permissions under the Vulnerabilities App - Asset Operational View resource.

scan-scanners.statement: The SecOps platform currently supports the Tenable Vulnerability Management and Tenable Security Center scanner outegrations for triggering scans, and scans can be triggered only on assets ingested from a source that has a corresponding outegration.

quotes: The SecOps platform currently supports the Tenable Vulnerability Management and the Tenable Security Center scanner outegrations.
Scans can be triggered only on assets ingested from a source that has a corresponding outegration configured.

scan-max-assets.statement: A maximum of 10 assets can be selected per scan.

quotes: A maximum of 10 assets can be selected per scan.
evidence.after: You can trigger scans for one or more assets directly from the Assets page.

scan-limits.statement: The number of concurrent scans is set by the Max Number of Parallel Scans setting in the scanner outegration; scans cannot be stopped in UVM and must be cancelled in the scanner interface.

quotes: The maximum number of scans that can run concurrently is determined by the Max Number of Parallel Scans setting in your scanner outegration configuration
Scans cannot be stopped in UVM after they are triggered. To cancel an ongoing scan, you must stop it directly through the scanner interface.

scan-flow.statement: The scanner queues and executes the scan job according to its own scheduling and capacity; the outegration automatically polls for final results and updates the asset data, with a possible short delay while queued ETL operations are processed; progress and completion can be monitored in the scanner outegration's activity log.

quotes: The scanner queues and executes the job according to its own scheduling and capacity.
the outegration automatically polls for final results and updates the corresponding asset data in the SecOps platform.
Results might be subject to a short delay while queued Extract, Transform, Load (ETL) operations are processed.
you can monitor its progress and completion status through the activity log for your scanner outegration.

drawer-tabs.title: What the asset and finding drawer tabs contain
drawer-tabs.detail: The captured articles name the default asset drawer tabs (Details, Asset Merging, Findings, Tickets) and finding drawer tabs (Details, Vulnerability, Finding Evidence) but do not describe the contents of the asset drawer tabs or the Details and Vulnerability tabs, or the Configuring Entity Drawers article. Fixes is a ticket drawer tab.
